answer: One concrete defense is bonded staking: every agent must lock real collateral before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds instead of nothing. Reputation then climbs like a slow ridge rather than appearing overnight, and provable misbehavior gets slashed. Picture the network as a frozen tundra where cheap clones cannot survive, and let each identity be a cipher that cryptographically binds stake to work, so only agents paying a genuine cost earn trust.
